This linux-x64 `ffmpeg` executable is a GPL build of FFmpeg 7.0.2-static.
Its `ffmpeg -version` banner and SHA-256 are recorded in `source.json`.
The banner configuration is longer than the earlier subset
`--enable-gpl --enable-version3 --enable-static --enable-libx264 --enable-libvpx`.
It still includes those flags, plus the other libraries named by the banner.

On 2026-11-09 the file matched the uncompressed bytes of
https://github.com/eugeneware/ffmpeg-static/releases/download/b6.1.1/ffmpeg-linux-x64.gz
(gzip SHA-256 bfe8a8fc511530457b528c48d77b5737527b504a3797a9bc4866aeca69c2dffa).
`UPSTREAM-README.txt` is the `linux-x64.README` asset from that same release.
It names build `ffmpeg-7.0.2-amd64-static.tar.xz` and lists library versions,
including libx264 and libvpx. That readme is not a source archive.

https://johnvansickle.com/ffmpeg/release-source/ was fetched the same day.
Its index did not contain an FFmpeg 7.0.2 tarball or those library versions.
Corresponding source is not in this repository, and this binary was not rebuilt
here. `correspondingSourceInRepo` and `rebuiltFromSource` stay false in
`source.json`.

`COPYING.GPLv3` matches the b6.1.1 `linux-x64.LICENSE` asset.
`COPYING.LGPLv2.1` is kept beside it. The executable is distributed under
GPL-3.0-or-later because the build uses `--enable-gpl` and `--enable-version3`.

Futureox Design ships it as a separate program at `Resources/bin/ffmpeg`
(Electron extraResource from `dist/bin`). The desktop host resolves that path
and the Rust sidecar spawns it with a fixed argument list. It is not linked
into the Electron or Rust binaries. Spawning this program does not decide the
license of the rest of the application.
